title: [BUG] OpenAIResponsesModel: tool-result documents (e.g. read_pdf) sent as file_url, rejected with 400 Failed to download file
body:
### Checks
- [x] I have updated to the latest minor and patch version of Strands (1.48.0, current on PyPI at time of filing)
- [x] I have checked the documentation and this is not expected behavior
- [x] I have searched issues and there are no duplicates of this one

### SDK Language
Python

### Strands Version
1.48.0

### Language Runtime Version
Python 3.14.0 (also reproduces on 3.11)

### Operating System
macOS 26 (Darwin 25.5.0)

### Installation Method
pip (via uv)

### Steps to Reproduce
Standalone repro, no agent needed — call the model's own formatting method directly and feed its output straight to the Responses API:

```python
import asyncio, os
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from strands.models.openai_responses import OpenAIResponsesModel

pdf_bytes = open("small.pdf", "rb").read()  # any small PDF

tool_result = {
    "toolUseId": "call_1",
    "status": "success",
    "content": [{"document": {"format": "pdf", "name": "test.pdf", "source": {"bytes": pdf_bytes}}}],
}
formatted = OpenAIResponsesModel._format_request_tool_message(tool_result)
print(formatted["output"][0])
# {'type': 'input_file', 'file_url': 'data:application/pdf;base64,...'}

client = AsyncOpenAI(api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"])

async def main():
    await client.responses.create(
        model="gpt-5.6-sol",  # any Responses-capable model
        input=[
            {"type": "function_call", "call_id": "call_1", "name": "read_pdf", "arguments": "{}"},
            {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "call_1", "output": formatted["output"]},
        ],
        tools=[{"type": "function", "name": "read_pdf", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}],
    )

asyncio.run(main())
```

In an actual agent, this reproduces whenever a tool (e.g. a `read_pdf`/`read_document`-style tool) returns a `document` content block as its `ToolResult` mid-conversation — the very next model call fails.

### Expected Behavior
The Responses API call succeeds; the model receives the PDF content via the tool result, same as when a document is attached directly to the initial user message.

### Actual Behavior
```
openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'Failed to download file.', 'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'param': 'url', 'code': 'invalid_value'}}
```

`_format_request_tool_message` (`strands-py/src/strands/models/openai_responses.py`, `document` branch) base64-encodes the document into a `data:` URL and sends it as `{"type": "input_file", "file_url": data_url}`. The Responses API treats `file_url` as a value it must fetch over the network, and a `data:` URI isn't a URL it can download — hence the 400.

Note `_format_request_message_content` (used for documents attached directly to a message, e.g. the initial context bundle) has the exact same bug via the exact same pattern — it's just less likely to be hit in practice since most integrations build the initial bundle themselves and can work around it downstream, whereas tool-result documents (returned by any custom `read_pdf`/file-reading tool) have no such escape hatch: they always go through `_format_request_tool_message`.

### Additional Context
Confirmed via a real multi-day A/B pipeline run (GPT-5.6 Sol vs. another provider) triaging ~30 documents per case: every run that reached a point where the model called a PDF-reading tool crashed with this exact error, reproducibly (two independent runs, same document, same failure). Downgrading `reasoning.effort` didn't change the outcome — this is a formatting bug, not a model/reasoning issue.

### Possible Solution
The Responses API's `input_file` part supports `file_data` (base64, with a `filename`) for embedded bytes — `file_url` is only for genuinely fetchable URLs. Both call sites should use `file_data` instead. I've opened a minimal PR that patches `_format_request_tool_message` only: #3674. `_format_request_message_content` has the identical latent bug (see above) but is out of scope for this PR since it isn't what this issue reproduces.

### Related Issues
None found.

linked_prs.title: fix(openai): send tool-result documents as file_data, not file_url
linked_prs.patch:
diff --git a/strands-py/src/strands/models/openai_responses.py b/strands-py/src/strands/models/openai_responses.py
index 20869ef7b6..55ff639839 100644
--- a/strands-py/src/strands/models/openai_responses.py
+++ b/strands-py/src/strands/models/openai_responses.py
@@ -779,7 +779,9 @@ def _format_request_tool_message(cls, tool_result: ToolResult) -> dict[str, Any]
                 has_media = True
                 doc = content["document"]
                 data_url = _encode_media_to_data_url(doc["source"]["bytes"], doc["format"], "document")
-                filename = doc.get("name", "document")
+                name = doc.get("name", "document")
+                suffix = f".{doc['format']}"
+                filename = name if name.endswith(suffix) else f"{name}{suffix}"
                 output_parts.append({"type": "input_file", "filename": filename, "file_data": data_url})
 
         # Return array if has media content, otherwise join as string for simpler text-only cases
diff --git a/strands-py/tests/strands/models/test_openai_responses.py b/strands-py/tests/strands/models/test_openai_responses.py
index a3c832c289..7048bfeda0 100644
--- a/strands-py/tests/strands/models/test_openai_responses.py
+++ b/strands-py/tests/strands/models/test_openai_responses.py
@@ -289,7 +289,7 @@ def test_format_request_tool_message_with_document():
     assert tru_result["output"][0]["filename"] == "test.pdf"
     assert "file_data" in tru_result["output"][0]
     assert "file_url" not in tru_result["output"][0]
-    assert tru_result["output"][1]["filename"] == "document"
+    assert tru_result["output"][1]["filename"] == "document.pdf"
